reviewers.summary: The filter sanitizes placeholder values, but a valid structured template can still carry raw prompt or document text in its literal portion.

findingList.message: Literal prompt or document text in a valid structured log template bypasses redaction and can reach log providers (OWASP A09:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: RenderMessage accepts a template when its placeholders are valid and bound, then returns the formatted message after only scrubbing bearer tokens and session cookies. It does not sanitize literal text surrounding placeholders.
evidence.failureScenario: A caller logs `Prompt: confidential lease clause {state}` with state `active`. The valid placeholder passes the template check, while the literal prompt text survives ScrubText and reaches the log provider. This exposes raw prompt or document text, contrary to the acceptance criteria (OWASP A09:2025).

reviewers.summary: The filter covers many named fields and common token patterns, but short content can pass through under operational names. The tests also cannot detect removal of a listed sensitive name.

findingList.message: Short prompt or document content under an operational property name bypasses redaction and can be exported.

evidence.codePathTraced: Sanitize keeps short, whitespace-free strings under operational names, and RenderMessage inserts those values into the emitted message.
evidence.failureScenario: If application code logs a one-word document excerpt such as `Confidential` as `{state}`, `state` is operational and the value passes through unchanged to the log provider. The same path can expose a one-word prompt in a trace tag named `status`, contrary to the requirement to keep raw prompts and document text out of every log and trace. OWASP A09:2025.

findingList.message: The tests do not fail when a listed property name is dropped, as acceptance criterion 4 requires.

evidence.codePathTraced: The listed names in SensitiveNamesAreRedacted are all non-operational, so Sanitize returns `[redacted]` for them through its default case even if the corresponding name is removed from SensitiveSegments.
evidence.failureScenario: If `prompt` is removed from the sensitive-name list, SensitiveNamesAreRedacted still passes because `prompt` is not operational, and the logging-pipeline test still sees it redacted by the default case. The suite therefore passes despite the regression, contrary to acceptance criterion 4.

reviewers.summary: The changed logging and tracing paths redact unapproved fields, sensitive property names, bearer tokens, and session cookies before forwarding records or trace attributes. I found no reachable security defect in the diff.
